biography: Orey Fidani’s racing journey began not on a track, but on the icy streets of Montreal. He spent his teenage years dodging snowbanks and outmaneuvering delivery trucks in his beat-up Civic, honing reflexes that would later serve him well. His raw talent was undeniable, but it was a chance encounter with a local karting team owner that truly ignited his career. The owner, impressed by Orey's aggressive style during an impromptu street race, offered him a spot on the team. From there, Orey devoured every opportunity, clawing his way through the ranks. A disastrous showing in his first F3 race, spinning out on the first lap, almost ended his dream before it began. But his relentless determination saw him bounce back stronger. Now, as a rising star with McLaren, Fidani is determined to prove he belongs among the elite.
drivingStyle: Fidani's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He attacks every corner with ferocious intensity, often pushing the car to its absolute limit. Tire management is not his forte; he prefers squeezing every last drop of performance out of the rubber, consequences be damned. This aggressive approach makes him a thrilling, if sometimes unpredictable, presence on the track. He thrives under pressure, relishing the challenge of overtaking in tight spaces, even if it means a bit of paint trading.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles; Rostova is known for her calculated precision, a direct contrast to Fidani's raw aggression. Their on-track battles are always intense.
A rivalry born from a controversial collision during a championship-deciding race, leaving both drivers with a bitter taste.
Bellini, a veteran driver, openly criticized Fidani's aggressive tactics, sparking a war of words and intense competition on the track.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Montreal Canadiens hat before every race.
Listens to a specific punk rock playlist to psych himself up.

famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, no matter what it takes."
careerHighlight: Winning the Canadian Grand Prix in his rookie season, an unexpected victory that cemented his status as a rising star and sent the home crowd into a frenzy.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the Monaco Grand Prix while leading, a costly mistake that robbed him of a potential victory and dented his confidence.
